_readme: ARIA api_queries.json: every Active IQ endpoint and query ARIA sends is defined in this file. The program has no endpoint URLs or query text of its own.

HOW IT IS USED: server.py (and launcher.py in the packaged app) read this file when they start and again whenever it changes on disk; the browser receives the same content from /aria-api.js (reload the page to pick up a change).
WHERE IT IS LOOKED FOR: a copy next to the executable is used first, then the copy bundled with the program.

SECTIONS: endpoints (base URLs), proxy (how local /api/... paths are forwarded), rest (named REST calls), graphql (named queries and mutations), fragments (reusable field lists), arguments (optional request arguments), rest_diagnostics (paths tried by the Settings diagnostics page).

PLACEHOLDERS: <<name>> is replaced by the value ARIA supplies when it sends the request (a cursor, a watchlist id, a serial number...). <<@NAME>> inserts the fragment NAME from "fragments". A placeholder with no value becomes empty text.
OPTIONAL ARGUMENTS: "arguments" holds snippets such as , after: "<<value>>". ARIA adds a snippet to the query only when it has a value for it (for example the cursor is empty on the first page).

TO CHANGE A FIELD LIST: edit the matching entry under "fragments". The systems queries are sent in three sizes (SYSTEMS_FIELDS_TAM, then _EFFICIENCY, then _MINIMAL): ARIA falls back to the next size when Active IQ rejects the larger one or its field-count limit is exceeded, so keep the smaller ones small.

TO ADD A QUERY: add an entry under "graphql" with a name, a description and the query text. Existing names are looked up by ARIA; a new name is only used by code that asks for it, so it is for experiments and for the diagnostics tools until a feature uses it.
TO POINT A CALL AT ANOTHER ENDPOINT: change "endpoints" (graphql, rest_base, graphql_v2) or the "path" of a "rest" entry.

AFTER EDITING: check that the file is valid JSON, then start a new sync. A syntax error in this file stops the server from calling Active IQ, and the server log names the file it loaded ("[API] Loaded API definitions from ...").
The "description" fields describe each entry; the program ignores them.

SCHEMA REFERENCE: these queries are written against the public Active IQ GraphQL schema reference on Apollo GraphOS Studio (see "schema_reference"). The engine reads them from this file; the program holds no query text. Run tools/validate_api_queries.py after editing a query to check it against the reference.

schema_reference.description: The public Active IQ GraphQL schema reference (Apollo GraphOS Studio). The queries in this file are written against it and the engine reads them from here; every entry was validated against the reference. Run tools/validate_api_queries.py to repeat the check.
schema_reference.result: Every query is validated against the public reference with tools/validate_api_queries.py, which reports the version of the reference it used each time it runs. The only entry that does not validate is "watchlists", a field the reference does not contain; the REST call rest.watchlist_list is used instead.

endpoints.description: graphql: main GraphQL endpoint used by the server. rest_base: REST host. graphql_v2: GraphQL endpoint on the REST host, used by the in-app query console.

proxy.description: The local server forwards /api/... requests from the browser to Active IQ. Paths in graphql_paths go to endpoints.graphql; other paths go to rest_base, with default_rest_version added when the path has no /vN prefix.

access_token.description: Exchanges the refresh token (<<refresh_token>>, stored in the local aiq_config.json) for a short-lived access token. Every GraphQL call then sends it as a Bearer token.

watchlist_list.description: Lists the account watchlists. The raw access token is sent in a header named authorizationToken (no Bearer prefix). The reply has the list under results.watchlist, with snake_case fields.

arguments.all_product_types: , productTypes: [FILER, SWApp, NON_FILER, UNKNOWN, SWITCH, AIDE_DCN]

arguments_descriptions.after: Paging cursor returned by the previous page.
arguments_descriptions.scope: Limits the query to one watchlist.
arguments_descriptions.product_types: Adds a productTypes filter with the list ARIA supplies.
arguments_descriptions.all_product_types: Adds all six product types: FILER, SWApp, NON_FILER, UNKNOWN, SWITCH, AIDE_DCN.
arguments_descriptions.nested_after: Offset for paging a nested list (LUNs, volumes, namespaces).
arguments_descriptions.sustainability_call_scoped: sustainabilityScore field limited to one watchlist.

fragment_descriptions.SYSTEMS_FIELDS_MINIMAL: Smallest systems field list: identity, customer, site, contract, software version, end of support and AutoSupport. Last fallback when the larger lists are rejected.
fragment_descriptions.SYSTEMS_FIELDS_TAM: Full systems field list, including capacity, efficiency, firmware, shelves, licenses and network ports for ONTAP systems. Tried first.
fragment_descriptions.SYSTEMS_FIELDS_EFFICIENCY: Medium systems field list: the full list without the utilization percentages and monthly capacity that can fail with null Float values, plus PVRs and downtime events. Second choice.
fragment_descriptions.ESERIES_CAP_FIELDS: Extra platform data fetched as its own pass (E-Series and StorageGRID capacity, power and heat, drives, upgrade history). Kept separate so the main query stays under Active IQ's field-count limit.
fragment_descriptions.ONTAP_EXTRA2_FIELDS: ONTAP-only second extra pass: adapter and FC inventory, Cloud Insights hosts, talking points. Separate because combined with the first extra pass it exceeds the field-count limit.
fragment_descriptions.LUN_VOLUME_FIELDS: LUN and volume inventory for ONTAP systems (counts, sizes, snapshot reserve, thin provisioning flag). The nested lists use pageSize 100000; <<nested_after>> pages them when a system has more. Volume sizes are in KiB. Active IQ has no igroup or LUN-to-host mapping data. Also requests per-volume protection settings (state, encryption, ARP, SnapLock mode, tiering policy, auto-size, percent used); ARIA turns them into per-system counts.
fragment_descriptions.SHELVES_SUMMARY_FIELDS: Shelf module counts and firmware currency. Fetched on its own because adding it to the main query exceeded the field-count limit.
fragment_descriptions.OTHER_PRODUCT_FIELDS: Fields for non-controller records (switches and similar products) that Active IQ also tracks.
fragment_descriptions.SUCCESS_PLAN_FIELDS: Success Plan fields: plan, objectives, milestones, actions, stakeholders and notes.
fragment_descriptions.OS_VERSION_FIELDS: OS version catalog fields: dates, support state, upgrade path and bundled firmware.
fragment_descriptions.CLUSTER_FIELDS: Cluster fields: identity, switches, shelves, SVMs with interfaces, capacity and monthly capacity.
fragment_descriptions.REPLACEMENT_FIELDS: Fields that replace deprecated ones: retentionSpecialist and solutionEngineerSpecialist (replace csm) and lifecycle eventDate (replaces daysToEvent). Fetched as its own pass because adding them to SYSTEMS_FIELDS_TAM exceeds Active IQ's field-count limit. The deprecated csm and daysToEvent stay in the main field lists as the fallback.
fragment_descriptions.MONTHLY_STATS_FIELDS: Monthly history for each ONTAP system: uptime and downtime seconds, volumes with ARP enabled, risks found and resolved (all, critical, CVE), carbon, and automatically resolved cases. Fetched as its own pass (the main systems field list is at the field-count limit). Months with no data come back empty or with zero totals.
fragment_descriptions.CAPACITY_ENERGY_FIELDS: Used capacity split into NAS, SAN and snapshots (ONTAP) and Active IQ's forecast power, carbon and heat (all platforms). A separate small pass, because adding them to the main lists exceeds Active IQ's field-count limit.

summary_watchlist.description: Fleet counts (systems, clusters, sites) for one watchlist. Used only for the log line at the start of a sync. Needs <<watchlist_id>>.
summary_watchlist.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

summary.description: Fleet counts for the whole account. Fails with a privilege error on accounts that lack unfiltered_system_access; the sync then counts from the data it fetches instead.
summary.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

watchlists.description: Watchlist list through GraphQL. This field is not in the current GraphQL schema, so the call normally fails and is ignored; the REST call rest.watchlist_list is the one that works. Kept in case the field is added.
watchlists.schema_check: field not in the public schema reference

systems_page.description: One page (100) of systems, including StorageGRID nodes. <<fields>> is a field list from "fragments"; <<after>> is the paging cursor, <<scope>> a watchlist, <<product_types>> an optional product-type filter. The first page is requested with no cursor.
systems_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

asar2_systems_page.description: Provisioned LUN and namespace size for ASA r2 systems only (ontapPersonalities: [ASAR2]). usableKiB on these objects reports bytes, not KiB; ARIA converts it. <<nested_after>> pages the nested lists (the value is an offset).
asar2_systems_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

clusters_page.description: One page (100) of clusters with switches, shelves, SVMs and capacity. Fields come from the CLUSTER_FIELDS fragment.
clusters_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

clusters_page_watchlist.description: Same as clusters_page, limited to one watchlist. Run for every watchlist to recover clusters the unscoped call does not return.
clusters_page_watchlist.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

risk_instances_page.description: One page (500) of risk instances with the risk details, the affected system and any acknowledgement.
risk_instances_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

cases_page.description: One page (200) of support cases. <<product_types>> adds all six product types (a plain query returns only controller records); ARIA retries without it if Active IQ rejects the argument.
cases_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

customers_page.description: One page (100) of customers with their sustainability score.
customers_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

recommendations.description: Top key recommendations (up to 1000) for a scope.
recommendations.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

recommendations_customer.description: Top key recommendations for one customer id.
recommendations_customer.query: { recommendations(isTopKeyRecommendation: true, limit: 1000, customerId: "<<customer_id>>") { recommendation rank category subCategory score } }
recommendations_customer.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

sites_page.description: One page (100) of sites with address and propensity counts.
sites_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

sustainability_score.description: Sustainability score history. <<call>> is sustainabilityScore, or sustainabilityScore(watchlistId: "...") for a scope (see "arguments").
sustainability_score.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

health_score_scope.description: The official Active IQ health score and its KPI breakdown for an account or watchlist scope.
health_score_scope.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

health_score_customer.description: The official health score for one customer group, identified by its NAGP id.
health_score_customer.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

success_plans_page.description: One page (200) of Success Plans grouped by customer group. The field list is the SUCCESS_PLAN_FIELDS fragment.
success_plans_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

os_versions_page.description: One page (500) of the ONTAP OS version catalog with bundled firmware. Field list: OS_VERSION_FIELDS.
os_versions_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

os_versions_by_name.description: OS catalog entries for specific versions that were not on the catalog pages. <<versions>> is a JSON list of version strings (ARIA sends 50 at a time).
os_versions_by_name.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

contract_renewals_page.description: One page (200) of systems with contract renewal data, for contracts ending between 2024-01-01 and 2030-12-31, across all six product types. Change the dates here to widen or narrow the window.
contract_renewals_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

aggregates_page.description: One page (200) of aggregates for one system (<<serial>>): name, root flag, FabricPool flag, storage efficiency and Active IQ's capacity forecast (monthly trend points, past and projected; the value is a fraction of allocated space, so 0.8 is 80%).
aggregates_page.query: { aggregates(pageSize: 200<<after>>, systemSerialNumber: "<<serial>>") { cursor aggregates { name isRoot raidType storageType offlineVolumesCount maxRaidSize snapLockMode isFabricPoolEnabled sisDisabledVolumesCount storageEfficiencyRatio { withoutSnapshot } capacityForecast { trend { year month tense usedAsPercentageOfAllocatedKB } } } } }
aggregates_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

watchlist_system_serials_page.description: One page (100) of system serial numbers in a watchlist. Used to build the watchlist membership list.
watchlist_system_serials_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

probe_per_system_firmware.description: Diagnostic: firmware fields for the first two systems. Used by the firmware probe button, not by a normal sync.
probe_per_system_firmware.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

probe_system_firmwares.description: Diagnostic: top-level systemFirmwares list (5 rows). Firmware probe only.
probe_system_firmwares.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

probe_drive_firmwares.description: Diagnostic: top-level driveFirmwares list (5 rows). Firmware probe only.
probe_drive_firmwares.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

probe_shelf_firmwares.description: Diagnostic: top-level shelfFirmwares list (5 rows). Firmware probe only.
probe_shelf_firmwares.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

probe_disk_qualification_packages.description: Diagnostic: top-level diskQualificationPackages list (5 rows). Firmware probe only.
probe_disk_qualification_packages.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

AckRisk.description: Write-back. Acknowledges a risk on a system in Active IQ. Sent only after the user confirms in the dialog and enters a justification.
AckRisk.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

MitigateRisk.description: Write-back. Records a risk mitigation. The schema accepts only the statuses SUCCESS and FAILURE and the tool CLOUD_MANAGER. Sent only after the user confirms. Active IQ marks the Risk Mitigation component as decommissioned, so this call may be rejected.
MitigateRisk.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

UpdateCQV.description: Write-back. Sets the Customer Qualified Version for a system. Sent only after the user confirms and gives a justification.
UpdateCQV.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

CreateCSP.description: Write-back. Creates a Success Plan. Sent only after the user confirms.
CreateCSP.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

UpdateCSP.description: Write-back. Updates a Success Plan. Sent only after the user confirms.
UpdateCSP.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

CloseCSP.description: Write-back. Closes a Success Plan by setting its status to CLOSED (the API has no delete). Sent only after the user confirms.
CloseCSP.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

risk_metadata_page.description: Metadata for risks by id (<<risk_ids>> is a JSON list, up to 100 ids): the kind of mitigation (configuration change, firmware or OS upgrade, hardware change or replacement), whether it is disruptive, whether it is public, playbook and fix-it availability, and bug references.
risk_metadata_page.query: { riskMeta(riskIds: <<risk_ids>>, pageSize: 100) { cursor riskMetadata { riskId mitigationAction mitigationActionSub mitigationCategory isPublic playbook hasUMFixit hasCloudManagerFixit burtReferences } } }
risk_metadata_page.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

case_summary.description: Support case counts (open and closed, by highest priority) and the trend over time, for an account or watchlist scope.
case_summary.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

risks_count.description: Active IQ's own risk, action, resolved-risk and system counts for an account or watchlist scope, in total and grouped by severity and by impact area.
risks_count.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

workload_summary.description: Volume counts and capacity by workload for an account or watchlist scope (data volumes only; ASA R2 systems are not included).
workload_summary.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference

sg_capacity_forecast.description: How many StorageGRID sites will pass 80% used capacity within 3, 6 and 12 months (Active IQ's forecast), with the site names.
sg_capacity_forecast.schema_check: validated against the public schema reference
